input: Calculate my combined rating for: 50% PTSD, 30% tinnitus, 20% back, 10% knee.
response:
Your combined rating is 80%.

VA does not add ratings together. It combines them one at a time, so each new rating applies only to the efficiency left after the earlier ones (38 CFR § 4.25).

Combining all ratings, largest first, each step rounded to a whole number (38 CFR § 4.25):
  Step 1: 50% combined with 30% = 65%
  Step 2: 65% combined with 20% = 72%
  Step 3: 72% combined with 10% = 75%
Combined value before final rounding: 75%
Rounded once, at the end, to the nearest 10 with a 5 going up (38 CFR § 4.25(b)): 80%

Check these figures with a Veterans Service Officer before relying on them.

input: Am I eligible for TDIU with one 60% rating and three 20% ratings?
response:
On these ratings, the percentage thresholds for TDIU in 38 CFR § 4.16(a) are met. Meeting them is not by itself entitlement to TDIU: VA must also find that you are unable to secure or follow a substantially gainful occupation because of your service-connected disabilities.

Your combined rating is 80%.

About your question on individual unemployability (TDIU):

38 CFR § 4.16(a) sets these percentage thresholds: "if there is only one such disability, this disability shall be ratable at 60 percent or more, and that, if there are two or more disabilities, there shall be at least one disability ratable at 40 percent or more, and sufficient additional disability to bring the combined rating to 70 percent or more".

Condition 1 is rated 60 percent, which meets the threshold for a single disability, if that is the only disability you rely on for unemployability. The threshold for two or more disabilities is also met: at least one condition is rated 40 percent or more and your combined rating is 80 percent.

For the one 60 percent or one 40 percent disability, 38 CFR § 4.16(a) says "the following will be considered as one disability": disabilities of one or both upper extremities or of one or both lower extremities (including the bilateral factor, if applicable), "disabilities resulting from common etiology or a single accident", "disabilities affecting a single body system", multiple injuries incurred in action, and multiple disabilities incurred as a prisoner of war. Vet-Rate does not evaluate these groupings, so the result above treats each condition separately.

The percentage is only one part. 38 CFR § 4.16(a) also requires that the person be "unable to secure or follow a substantially gainful occupation as a result of service-connected disabilities", "in the judgment of the rating agency". Vet-Rate cannot determine that.

VA does not add ratings together. It combines them one at a time, so each new rating applies only to the efficiency left after the earlier ones (38 CFR § 4.25).

Combining all ratings, largest first, each step rounded to a whole number (38 CFR § 4.25):
  Step 1: 60% combined with 20% = 68%
  Step 2: 68% combined with 20% = 74%
  Step 3: 74% combined with 20% = 79%
Combined value before final rounding: 79%
Rounded once, at the end, to the nearest 10 with a 5 going up (38 CFR § 4.25(b)): 80%

Check these figures with a Veterans Service Officer before relying on them.

This answer covers your combined rating and the 38 CFR § 4.16(a) percentage thresholds. It does not say whether you are unemployable, which VA decides. If you also asked about something else, such as how to apply or monthly pay, please ask it as a separate question.

input: Can I qualify for TDIU with only one 60% mental health rating?
response:
On these ratings, the percentage thresholds for TDIU in 38 CFR § 4.16(a) are met. Meeting them is not by itself entitlement to TDIU: VA must also find that you are unable to secure or follow a substantially gainful occupation because of your service-connected disabilities.

Your combined rating is 60%.

About your question on individual unemployability (TDIU):

38 CFR § 4.16(a) sets these percentage thresholds: "if there is only one such disability, this disability shall be ratable at 60 percent or more, and that, if there are two or more disabilities, there shall be at least one disability ratable at 40 percent or more, and sufficient additional disability to bring the combined rating to 70 percent or more".

Mental health is rated 60 percent, which meets the threshold for a single disability.

For the one 60 percent or one 40 percent disability, 38 CFR § 4.16(a) says "the following will be considered as one disability": disabilities of one or both upper extremities or of one or both lower extremities (including the bilateral factor, if applicable), "disabilities resulting from common etiology or a single accident", "disabilities affecting a single body system", multiple injuries incurred in action, and multiple disabilities incurred as a prisoner of war. Vet-Rate does not evaluate these groupings, so the result above treats each condition separately.

The percentage is only one part. 38 CFR § 4.16(a) also requires that the person be "unable to secure or follow a substantially gainful occupation as a result of service-connected disabilities", "in the judgment of the rating agency". Vet-Rate cannot determine that.

VA does not add ratings together. It combines them one at a time, so each new rating applies only to the efficiency left after the earlier ones (38 CFR § 4.25).

Combining: only one rating to carry forward (60%), so there is nothing to combine.
Combined value before final rounding: 60%
Rounded once, at the end, to the nearest 10 with a 5 going up (38 CFR § 4.25(b)): 60%

Check these figures with a Veterans Service Officer before relying on them.
